text: Gold fell about 1% overnight to near $3,845 and briefly touched about $3,830, its lowest since October 2025, as Fed hike bets and a firm dollar weighed.
Silver dropped further to about $47.50, so the gold/silver ratio rose to about 81; this matters for SLV and AGQ, which closed Friday at $44.13 and $42.43.
Treasury yields eased slightly before Fed Chair Warsh speaks at 9 AM PT: the 10-year was near 5.13% and the 2-year near 4.84%.
Japan's economy was flat in the third quarter (−0.1% annualized, weaker than expected), but USD/JPY held just under 160 at about 159.5 on intervention warnings.
Nasdaq-100 futures were down about 1% as Nvidia fell premarket ahead of Tuesday's results; this matters for QQQ, TQQQ and SQQQ.
The New York Fed's factory survey reportedly fell to 7.8 in November, well below the 17.6 expected.
Brent was mixed in the mid-$90s as worries about a supply surplus met news of an Iranian strike on a US base in Bahrain; this matters for NRGU.
Bitcoin slid to about $64,000, roughly 6.5% below Friday's level, amid Fed hike worries and ETF outflows.
